solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Most untidy officers' area that is beside street

parts.note: the mess is where military officers eat and relax together
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for 'that is'

explanation.surface: A grumble about the sloppiest bit of the barracks, the officers' quarters right by the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A superlative adjective: the untidiest thing is the most disordered and cluttered of all.

clue.text: Error from teacher upset her favourite?

parts.note: Miss is how British schoolchildren address a female teacher

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: the teacher's pet is her favourite pupil

explanation.surface: The class pet has been put out by the teacher, who seems to have made a slip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'her' just points back to the teacher, linking Miss and her pet in the surface; it supplies no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a false step or blunder is an error.

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
a pain is an annoying nuisance

explanation.surface: A minor irritation encountered while abroad somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an Iberian nation in southwest Europe is a country.

indicators.note: distraught means deeply agitated and upset, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: The men's rudeness leaves the person on the receiving end very upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: cheeky, disrespectful behaviour is rudeness.

clue.text: Classes very restless, teacher stressed at first

parts.note: so means very, as in 'so tired'

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of each of these three words is used

explanation.surface: School classes are very fidgety and the teacher is stressed from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' takes R, T and S from restless, teacher, stressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: kinds or categories are classes.

definitions.meaning: deserted or gone away from, as in a job one walked out of
port is the larboard side of a ship, facing forward

explanation.definitionFit: Two unrelated senses: a past participle meaning deserted, and the nautical side of a vessel opposite starboard.

clue.text: Understanding French in shelter ultimately possible

parts.note: en is the French word for in
a tent is a canvas shelter

indicators.note: ultimately means only the final letter of possible is used

explanation.surface: Reaching an agreement with the French while camped under cover may finally be possible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives E, the last letter of possible.
explanation.definitionFit: A friendly understanding or informal alliance between nations, as in the Entente Cordiale.

parts.note: to tire is to grow weary

explanation.surface: A tired English visitor on a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: TIREE is an island in the Inner Hebrides off Scotland's west coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a low, windswept Hebridean island off the west coast of Scotland.

clue.text: Once felled e.g. can become subject of myth

indicators.note: can become signals that these letters may change into a different word by rearrangement

explanation.surface: A tree, once cut down, may turn into the stuff of legend.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Jason and the Argonauts sought this ram's prize in Greek legend, so it is a subject of myth.

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for South
camp means exaggerated, theatrical or affected in manner

explanation.surface: A description of a mischief-maker who came up from the south putting on airs.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a mischievous child or rogue is a little rascal.

indicators.note: absorbing means the duty list takes another letter into its middle

parts.note: a roster is a list of people on duty

indicators.note: initially says only the opening letter of Oscar is used

explanation.surface: A farmyard roll-call of poultry that happens to include a bird named Oscar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absorbing' puts O, the first letter of Oscar from 'initially', inside ROSTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the cockerel is a male domestic fowl, so the general bird term covers it.

parts.note: ta is British informal thanks, as is cheers
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A knight raises a glass to toast what the sunshine has done.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is everyday British slang for thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposure to sunshine browns the skin, so a bronzed skin colour is what the sun produces.

indicators.note: brewing suggests ingredients being worked up and mixed, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone notices apple cider being made at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a dwelling place or house where one lives is one's home.

clue.text: On return, refer to work in verse

indicators.note: on return means the pieces that follow are read backwards

parts.note: to cite a source is to refer to it
op is short for opus, a musical or literary work

explanation.surface: Instructions to quote a piece of writing in poetry when it comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On return' covers both words together, so the whole two-word string is read backwards, not each word separately.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective for language written in metre or with poetry's qualities, as 'in verse' describes.

clue.text: Creator of secret message enclosed on German river

indicators.note: on in a down clue means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: enc. is the abbreviation for enclosed, seen on letters
the Oder flows along Germany's border with Poland

explanation.surface: A spy's coded note enclosed somewhere along a German river.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone or something that turns plain text into cipher creates secret messages.

parts.note: in means at home, as in 'staying in'
SE is the compass abbreviation for southeast
CT is the US postal abbreviation for Connecticut

explanation.surface: An address of sorts: perhaps fly back to a house in the southeastern corner of Connecticut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' marks the definition as an example: a fly is one kind of six-legged creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a housefly is one of countless six-legged bugs, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: Game of chance has time for learner, unsteady

indicators.note: time for learner means one letter is swapped in where the other stood

parts.note: a lottery is a game of chance decided by drawn numbers
L is the learner abbreviation, from British L-plates

explanation.surface: A gambler, unsteady on their feet, plays a game of chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has time for learner' swaps T for the L of LOTTERY; L is from the L-plate on a British learner driver's car.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: shaky and wobbly on one's feet is unsteady.

parts.note: a buck is a male deer, rabbit or similar animal

indicators.note: adjusted means the letters of flute are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A man fiddles with his flute, then thinks about how much a container holds.
explanation.definitionFit: The amount a pail holds is its full measure, so the quantity is the vessel's capacity.

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the run of these two words

explanation.surface: A hat bought from a shopkeeper in Aube, a French département.
explanation.walkthrough: The '?' nods to the French setting: a soft flat cap is famously French.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a soft round flat cap is a piece of headwear.

clue.text: Iron also reduced inside? Not true

indicators.note: inside means the shortened word goes within the iron symbol

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

indicators.note: reduced means the word also is cut short by its last letter

explanation.surface: Asking whether iron has also been reduced inside, chemically, then declaring it untrue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron' and 'reduced' suggest chemistry, but 'reduced' just docks the last letter and 'inside' places the remainder within the element's symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: untrue or incorrect, as a statement can be.

definitions.meaning: a nocturnal flying mammal comes out after dark
a club used to strike the ball in cricket or baseball

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a nocturnal winged mammal and the wooden implement used to hit a ball in cricket.

definitions.meaning: Sir Anthony, the art historian and one of the Cambridge Five who spied for the USSR

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: frank and plain-spoken, and the surname of the Cambridge spy ring's art historian member.

definitions.meaning: in mathematics and chemistry, a root or base form, as in square root sign or an atom group
someone holding far-reaching or revolutionary political views

explanation.definitionFit: The word comes from Latin radix, root, giving the mathematical root sign, and also names a person wanting sweeping change.

clue.text: Dodge real hurdles on regular basis

indicators.note: on a regular basis means taking every other letter of these two words, starting with the second

explanation.surface: A hurdler skips round genuine obstacles rather than jumping them, as a matter of routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on regular basis' takes the 2nd, 4th, 6th, 8th and 10th letters of 'real hurdles'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to evade or escape something by quickness is to dodge it.

clue.text: Such an accountant, earthy of course

definitions.meaning: a bookmaker was once politely called an accountant of the racecourse grass in Britain
the grassy soil surface of a racecourse, which is earthy

explanation.walkthrough: A 'turf accountant' is an old British euphemism for a bookmaker who takes bets on horse races.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the word that precedes 'accountant' for a bookie, and the grass-and-soil surface a racecourse is made of.

clue.text: Tips on rare case, not likely, used not long ago

indicators.note: tips are the end letters, so the first and last letters of each of the four words are taken

explanation.surface: Advice about an unusual legal case that seems improbable, used only lately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tips on' takes the outside letters: RE, CE, NT, LY.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverb synonym: something done lately happened not long ago.
